# cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service (Resource)

Switches on Cleura's **Recovery service** (disaster recovery) for a **block volume**. The volume
itself is usually managed by the OpenStack provider's
[`openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3`](https://registry.terraform.io/providers/terraform-provider-openstack/openstack/latest/docs/resources/blockstorage_volume_v3).
This resource adds the Recovery service to it by ID, so the two providers work side by side.

- `retention_days` and `immutable` are changed in place, without switching the service off.
- If the service is already on for the volume, creating this resource takes it over and applies the
  configured settings.
- Destroying the resource switches the service off. Terraform then waits, for up to 30 minutes,
  until Cleura has finished stopping it, so a `terraform destroy` that also deletes the volume works
  in one run.

~> **Recovery points:** destroying this resource, or removing it from your configuration, switches
the service off, and the volume's recovery points may then be deleted. For volumes whose recovery
points you can't afford to lose, consider `lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }`.

~> **Immutable recovery points** (`immutable = true`) may prevent changing or switching off the
service until their retention has passed.

### Moving from other tooling

If other tooling switched the service on, create this resource for the volume, or import it. Then
remove the other tooling's state **without** destroying it, because destroying it would switch the
service off. In Terraform, use a `removed` block with `lifecycle { destroy = false }`, or
`terraform state rm`.

### Prerequisites

The provider must be authenticated and have a `region`. The volume's project defaults to the
provider's `project_id`; set `project_id`, and `region` if needed, on the resource when the volume
lives elsewhere. See the provider's [Authentication](../index.md#authentication) documentation.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    cleura = {
      source = "cleura/cleura"
    }
    openstack = {
      source = "terraform-provider-openstack/openstack"
    }
  }
}

# The volume, managed by the OpenStack provider. Its volume type must support
# the Recovery service.
resource "openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3" "data" {
  name        = "data"
  size        = 100
  volume_type = "cbs"
}

# Switch on the Recovery service for the volume and keep recovery points for
# 10 days (10 or 30).
resource "cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service" "data" {
  volume_id      = openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3.data.id
  retention_days = 10
}
```

To protect several volumes, use `for_each`:

```terraform
resource "cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service" "disks" {
  for_each = openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3.disks

  volume_id      = each.value.id
  retention_days = 30
}
```

## Import

```shell
# A Recovery service is imported by its volume's ID. Region and project default
# to the provider's; prefix them as <project_id>/<volume_id> or
# <region>/<project_id>/<volume_id> to name them explicitly.
terraform import cleura_openstack_volume_recovery_service.data 5c9a1f0e-2b3d-4e5f-8a6b-7c8d9e0f1a2b
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `retention_days` (Number) How many days recovery points are kept: `10` or `30`. Changed in place.
- `volume_id` (String) ID of the volume, for example `openstack_blockstorage_volume_v3.data.id`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `immutable` (Boolean) Whether recovery points are immutable. Defaults to `false`. Changed in place. Immutable recovery points may prevent later changes, and destroying this resource, until their retention has passed.
- `project_id` (String) OpenStack project of the volume. Defaults to the provider's `project_id`. Changing it forces a new resource.
- `region` (String) Region of the volume. Defaults to the provider's `region`. Changing it forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The volume's ID.
- `started_at` (String) When the Recovery service was switched on (RFC 3339).
